newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks rise in morning, boosted by rate outlook.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks rise in morning, boosted by rate outlook.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks advanced in Monday morning trade as expectations of steady interest rates lifted prices, particularly in the banking and property sector.
The Hang Seng Index was up 81.43 points, or 0.61 percent, at 13,403.22. Turnover was HK$2.21 billion after the first hour of trade.

"The long bond yield has come down a little bit and apparently there is not much concern that there will be a change in interest rates at the FOMC (Federal Open Market Committee) meeting," said Kent Rossiter, institutional sales manager at Nikko Securities.
The U.S. Fed policy setting body meets on Tuesday and Wednesday.

U.S. bonds rallied ahead of the meeting, with the benchmark 30-year Treasury bond gaining 1-1/32 on Friday to yield 6.79 percent. Brokers said recent economic data pointed to a steady near-term interest rate outlook.
However, Patrick Chia, research director at China Everbright Research, said the Hang Seng was likely to run into resistance at around 13,500 points.
"Investors are still cautious about the (U.S.) jobs figures," he said.
The U.S. January jobs report is due on Friday.

Shares in Great Eagle Holdings gained HK$0.60 to HK$32.00, boosted by the company's announcement that it planned to spin off its Tai Shan unit, raising between HK$2.31 billion and HK$2.50 billion. The news had been widely expected by the market, brokers said.
Bank of East Asia fell HK$0.70 to HK$34.20. The company is due release its 1996 results later on Monday.
"People expect about 12 percent growth (in net profit)," said Rossiter.
However, shares in HSBC Holdings rose HK$2.00 to HK$181.50 while Hang Seng Bank gained HK$0.75 to HK$92.00.
Two companies made their stock market debuts on Monday.
Consumer electronics products maker Chun Tai Holdings received an enthusiastic welcome, opening at HK$1.30 compared with an issue price of HK$1.03 and later rising to a high of HK$1.58.
Shui On Construction and Materials made a less impressive debut, opening at HK$9.45 compared with an issue price of HK$9.30 per share and later falling back to HK$8.55.
In the property sector, Sun Hung Kai Properties rose HK$1.25 to HK$88.75 and Cheung Kong gained HK$1.00 to HK$73.25.
